requirement: Hold database connection settings with a password that is masked in reprs and log output, build a connection URL with the password percent-encoded, offer a redacted URL for logging, and validate the host and port range.
skeleton: A frozen DatabaseConfig model with Field bounds and a SecretStr password, url() quoting the unwrapped secret with an empty safe set, redacted_url() with a placeholder, and log_fields dumping in json mode.
caption: PostgreSQL connection settings in pydantic v2 that keep the password secret. DatabaseConfig is frozen through ConfigDict and has host, user and database as str with Field min_length=1, port defaulting to 5432 with ge=1 and le=65535, and password typed as pydantic.SecretStr, so repr and str print asterisks instead of the value. url() unwraps the secret with get_secret_value and percent-encodes it with urllib.parse.quote using safe set to an empty string, so @, / and : in the password cannot break the URL, then builds postgresql://user:password@host:port/database. redacted_url() builds the same URL with *** in place of the password for log lines. log_fields(config) returns model_dump with mode json: a SecretStr dumps as the masked string of ten asterisks, so the dict is safe to hand to a structured logger. Invalid settings raise pydantic.ValidationError. The fixture asserts that the password p@ss/w:rd never appears in repr or str, that log_fields returns the exact dict with the masked password and default port, that url() encodes the password as p%40ss%2Fw%3Ard, that redacted_url() uses *** with port 6543, that ports 0 and 65536 raise ValidationError while 65535 is accepted, and that an empty host raises ValidationError.

constraints: The password never appears in repr or str
Log fields show the password as asterisks
The URL percent-encodes every special character in the password
The redacted URL replaces the password with ***

rationale.teaches: SecretStr with explicit get_secret_value at the single point of use, json-mode dumps for masked logging, and quote(safe='') for credentials in URLs.
rationale.why: A plain str password leaks through any repr, traceback or log call, and default quoting leaves / in place, which only breaks with real passwords.

ops.docstring: Database settings that keep the password out of reprs and log records.

ops.stmt: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, SecretStr

ops.source:
class DatabaseConfig(BaseModel):
    """Connection settings for a PostgreSQL database."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    host: str = Field(min_length=1)
    port: int = Field(default=5432, ge=1, le=65535)
    user: str = Field(min_length=1)
    password: SecretStr
    database: str = Field(min_length=1)

    def url(self) -> str:
        """The full connection URL, with the password percent-encoded."""
        password = quote(self.password.get_secret_value(), safe="")
        return (
            f"postgresql://{self.user}:{password}"
            f"@{self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database}"
        )

    def redacted_url(self) -> str:
        """The connection URL with the password replaced, safe for logs."""
        return f"postgresql://{self.user}:***@{self.host}:{self.port}/{self.database}"

candidates.why_wrong: A plain str password shows up in repr, str and the log fields.
quote keeps / unescaped by default, so the password splits the URL path.
lt=65535 rejects the highest valid port number.
An empty host is accepted and produces a broken URL.
Python-mode dumps return a SecretStr object instead of the masked string.
